html:
RIFE (Practical-RIFE 4.25, 4.26 and 4.25 lite, Huang et al.): makes the frame between two video frames from the optical flow it estimates between them, for slow motion and higher frame rates. MIT code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Paper: Real-Time Intermediate Flow Estimation for Video Frame Interpolation, ECCV 2022, 2020-11-12
  • Original code: https://github.com/hzwer/Practical-RIFE at bbfd2ea90910
  • Code licence: MIT (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: MIT
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/hzwer/Practical-RIFE/blob/bbfd2ea90910789a860ea3e2b32a240cd577b75e/README.md ; https://github.com/hzwer/Practical-RIFE/blob/bbfd2ea90910789a860ea3e2b32a240cd577b75e/LICENSE
  • Training data: Vimeo-90K (septuplets / triplets for frame interpolation) (The README does not list the training data of the 4.x releases; the RIFE paper (arXiv:2011.06294) trains on Vimeo-90K, the 4.x releases add unnamed data (anime scenes per the 4.25 release note).)
  • Options: cuda_graphs = True (speed only)
  • Kernel libraries: cudnn_hacc
  • Variants: rife-4.25, rife-4.26, rife-4.25-lite
  • Outputs: frame
  • Input size: any H x W >= 128, padded to a multiple of 128
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): rife-4.25 3000x4000 (5.5 GiB peak allocated, 6.8 reserved); rife-4.26 3000x4000 (5.5 GiB peak allocated, 6.8 reserved); rife-4.25-lite 3000x4000 (5.5 GiB peak allocated, 6.5 reserved)
  • rife-4.25 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 36 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 56 s (ONNX + engine).
  • rife-4.26 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 35 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 55 s (ONNX + engine).
  • rife-4.25-lite 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 35 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 50 s (ONNX + engine).
  • rife-4.25 original 1080x1920: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream Practical-RIFE Model.inference, timestep 0.5, zero pad to 128, inference_video.py --fp16: half default dtype, model and input
  • rife-4.26 original 1080x1920: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream Practical-RIFE Model.inference, timestep 0.5, zero pad to 128, inference_video.py --fp16: half default dtype, model and input
  • rife-4.25-lite original 1080x1920: the authors' mixed-precision option (float16); upstream Practical-RIFE Model.inference, timestep 0.5, zero pad to 128, inference_video.py --fp16: half default dtype, model and input
  • rife-4.25 load / first call: original 1.42 s / 0.265 s, portable 0.31 s / 0.491 s, kernels 1.5 s / 0.203 s
  • rife-4.26 load / first call: original 0.18 s / 0.046 s, portable 0.78 s / 0.243 s, kernels 1.15 s / 0.198 s
  • rife-4.25-lite load / first call: original 0.18 s / 0.12 s, portable 1.0 s / 0.229 s, kernels 1.11 s / 0.183 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

DAVIS 2017 trainval 480p (JPEG), frames 0 / 2 and 20 / 22 of each of the 90 videos give the frame 1 / 21 at time 0.5, compared with the real one: PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) of the output rounded to uint8, on RGB in [0, 1], averaged over the triplets. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.0001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.00024 and p99 <= 0.0013 (absolute error of the output frame).
